name: Conchoidal Fracture
desc: A flint core being knapped, blow by blow — glassy stone breaks in shells, so every strike drives a Hertzian cone that peels a flake away and leaves a hollow bulb of percussion behind it, ringed with concentric ripple marks that widen as they run and combed with fine radial hackle, each fresh scar slicing clean through the older ones while the chalky white cortex creeps back over everything the knapper has not touched lately.

energy.doc: relief gain, lustre and tonal contrast — max lights the ripples hard and fires the specular

scale.doc: magnification into the core about the x/y anchor — max nearly triples the ripple marks

speed.doc: how fast the knapper works — strike rate and how quickly each crack front runs out

density.doc: coarse or fine knapping: 0 is a few big bold flakes, 1 is rapid small pressure-flaking

cortex.doc: how much chalky white rind survives on the core — the material contrast against fresh black flint

hue.doc: hue of the stone — warm honey chert through cold grey flint

x.doc: horizontal position of the magnified region

y.doc: vertical position of the magnified region

style.doc: aesthetic: grey-black glassy flint with chalk cortex under a raking lamp / jet obsidian where form comes from gloss alone / honey-banded chert whose bedding is genuinely sliced open by the fracture surface / archaeological lithic drawing in pure stipple and engraved contour / radiographic negative with the ripples glowing

seed.doc: deterministic seed for the nodule, cortex patches and the sequence of blows
